title: Architecture / database / backend repository case studies
verification_method: GitHub REST API (license, archived flag, default branch HEAD SHA, tags, latest release) + official project sites/docs; no cloning or execution. SHAs are 12-char prefixes of full SHAs at fetch time (full SHA recorded for eshop).
license_warning: License state is point-in-time and per-version-band (see redis). Always re-verify before redistribution or derivative use.

cases.license_note: GitHub API reports NOASSERTION because the license is the project's own PostgreSQL License; OSI-approved.
cases.lifecycle: active; major release annually, 5-year support per major. PostgreSQL 18 GA 2025-09-25 (async I/O, UUIDv7, virtual generated columns); current minor 18.6 (2026-08-13); 19 GA planned 2026-11-19.

key_paths.src/backend/access/heap/: heapam: MVCC tuple visibility (HOT updates, hint bits)
key_paths.src/backend/access/transam/: WAL (xlog), MVCC snapshots, transaction status (CLOG), SSI (predicate locking)
key_paths.src/bin/pg_waldump/: inspect WAL records — pairs with ARIES study
key_paths.src/backend/storage/async/: new in PG18: asynchronous I/O subsystem
key_paths.doc/src/sgml/mvcc.sgml: MVCC chapter source: transaction isolation, visibility rules, SSI — the normative operational semantics doc
key_paths.doc/src/sgml/monitoring.sgml: monitoring chapter source: statistics collector, pg_stat_* views, progress reporting — the observability surface
key_paths.doc/src/sgml/pgstatstatements.sgml: pg_stat_statements reference: normalized-query execution statistics — the tuning evidence source
key_paths.doc/src/sgml/ref/pgbench.sgml: pgbench reference: built-in repeatable load generator for before/after tuning runs
key_paths.doc/src/sgml/ref/pg_basebackup.sgml: pg_basebackup reference: physical base backup underpinning PITR (restore + WAL replay to a recovery target)

cases.learn: Full modular DBMS internals: storage, MVCC+VACUUM, WAL recovery, cost-based optimization, extensibility (index AMs, hooks, FDWs), SSI serializable.
cases.cannot_learn: Managed-service operational tuning (RDS/CloudSQL parameter folklore), which lives outside source.
